html:
SMTO-CMP-0020 — SMTO couldn't confirm it saved what you asked it to remember

GUID: f0633d68-b1af-4541-a0cc-c588698aa333
Slug: completion-memory-persistence-required
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • You asked SMTO to remember something, but it hasn't confirmed saving it to Memory, so it won't call the task finished. Other work in the task is kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Agent behavior › Knowledge, select Open Memory Editor, and look for what you asked SMTO to remember. If it's already there, SMTO only needs to confirm the save rather than add it twice.
  2. If it's missing, select Resume, or ask SMTO to save it to Memory in the "Continue this conversation" box under the task, then select Continue. SMTO needs a confirmed Memory save before it can call this task finished.
  3. If you no longer need it saved, type "Don't save this" in the message box under the task and send it. That message removes the save request, so it no longer blocks finishing the task.

What success looks like

  • The item appears in Memory Editor and the task shows Completed.

If it still fails

  • If Memory Editor shows an error or the save keeps failing, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Check whether the earlier action already happened in Memory Editor before asking again, so you don't create duplicates.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The task explicitly requested Memory persistence, but the recorded successful plus no-op Memory writes are below memory_persistence_min_writes (reason memory_persistence_required).

What this means

  • The task explicitly requests Memory persistence but recorded successful/no-op Memory writes are below memory_persistence_min_writes. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • The task explicitly requests Memory persistence but recorded successful/no-op Memory writes are below memory_persistence_min_writes.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect explicit persistence intent and write/no-op counters with their returned key/revision evidence.

How to fix it

  • Inspect memory_explicit_request, memory_persistence_min_writes and the memory_writes and memory_noop_writes counters in the run's memory_diagnostics, plus any memory.put receipts and their returned key and revision (require_persistence in src/agent_runtime/skills/memory/diagnostics.py). Confirm the Memory store is available, then complete one successful memory.put and cite it, or report blocked or partial if Memory is unavailable; do not replay other completed work.
  • Complete the required Memory persistence and verify its returned revision before claiming it was saved.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The required supported Memory write is confirmed; optional learning alone does not block completion.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
